Site has race catalog, free tools (marathon time predictor, fueling calculator, race-readiness quiz, shoe finder), blog, /download.
Installs of the free app; secondary: tool usage and race-catalog engagement that lead to installs
Free sources only (Google Autocomplete gl=in, Google Trends relative, manual SERP reading). No Ahrefs/Similarweb/paid credits.
Keywords are never filtered or weighted by the site's existing content or GSC rankings. Existing pages enter only in Phase 10 (mapping), after scoring.
1-5 on seven dimensions; HIGHER IS ALWAYS BETTER (competition_ease 5 = weak SERP).
How directly the query's need is solved by the product (5 = core, 1 = unrelated)
Search-interest proxy (1-4 from autocomplete breadth; Trends probe can override). NOT volume. 5 only with real evidence.
Closeness to action: tool/commercial 5, plan-seeking/commercial-investigation 4, informational 3, navigational 1-2
Manual SERP read: 5 = thin/low-authority/gap, 1 = big publishers + apps dominate
Quality of the content gap an Orka page could fill (5 = nobody answers it well)
Likelihood a visitor converts to install / becomes an engaged user
How much real evidence backs the scores (autocomplete-only = low)
relevance .20, demand .15, intent .15, competition .15, opportunity .15, value .15, confidence .05
demand_heavy, value_heavy, low_competition, equal. A cluster is 'weight-sensitive' if its rank moves >4 places across sets.

1) NO absolute search volumes anywhere. 2) SERP checks used a US-only search tool, not google.co.in; India SERPs will differ. 3) Autocomplete shows what Google suggests, not how often it is searched. 4) Google Trends could not be re-run from the cloud container (proxy returns 403); only the earlier 5-term probe exists. 5) Competition and opportunity are one analyst's manual ratings.
